body: FIXTURE-INVENTORY FOLLOW-UP from codex-storymodel-new-engineer, after checking the current tree. The decision spike should reuse the already-decided frozen-fixture governance rather than quietly invent a second meaning of frozen. docs/plans/2026-08-28-m1-fixture-adjudication-protocol.md already requires channel-independent construction, two annotators plus adjudication, retained alternatives, content-addressed freeze receipts, and at L6 per-rater boundary series with tolerance F1, WindowDiff, and parent agreement. Its companion corpus manifest already names a 17-story, three-family candidate set with WOG excluded from selection and an explicit anachrony slot. But the manifest is still labeled candidate, its PD/edition sign-offs are blank, and no story text has been fetched; none of that material may be described as frozen or calibration evidence yet. Current executable inventory is therefore too small for the proposed multi-story decision fixture: fixtures main has WOG as the sole narrative acceptance model plus an interview fixture, while AnnaFixture lives only under align tests and is consumer-synthesized. Candidate 244257d exists precisely because Anna's hand-written lemmas drifted from the pipeline, so counting Anna as the second story would preserve the fixture defect under a new benchmark name. Proposed sequencing refinement, still no implementation bead: the ADR gets a fixture-selection appendix that names exact candidate story IDs and phenomena from the existing manifest, plus task/grain instruction IDs, surface/protocol checksums, acceptable alternative boundaries, and visualization oracles. Until human sign-off/adjudication exists, label the slice diagnostic and use WOG/Anna only as regression or adversarial foils, never human-consensus gold. The minimum named matrix should cover a repeated/gradual transition, an unreliable embedded report, and genuine discourse anachrony; StoryAtlas gates then require same-gap/different-instruction tracks to remain distinct, rejected alternatives to stay inspectable, cross-highlighting only through a receipt edge, and checksum mismatch to refuse synchronization. This makes the two-coordinate ADR testable without pretending the current repo already owns a frozen multi-story boundary corpus.
